instruments.statusNote: A bill sent to the Assembly in February 2026 would show the IVA separately on invoices (tax-exclusive pricing), fixing its effective rate at 13% instead of about 14.94%. It had not been confirmed as law at the check date.

taxes.base: Habitual sales of movable goods, services and works contracts, leasing and definitive imports.
taxes.payer: Consumers; businesses charge and credit it against tax on purchases.

rate.headline: 13% of the net sale price
details: The 13% is currently included in the invoice price, so the effective rate is about 14.94% of the price before tax.
Exports and certain imports of capital goods are exempt.

instruments.explanation: The largest tax in Bolivia. The figure used here is the SIN's domestic VAT; VAT on imports is collected by customs.
exceptions: Numerous exemptions apply to books, diplomatic imports, exports and some tourism services.

names.official: Impuesto sobre las Utilidades de las Empresas (IUE)
names.native: Impuesto sobre las Utilidades de las Empresas

taxes.base: Net taxable profit of public and private companies, including sole proprietorships, and profits of foreign beneficiaries.

rate.headline: 25% of net taxable profit; higher for some sectors
details: Additional rates apply to financial entities and mining companies.
Remittances of profits abroad bear 12.5% (IUE-BE).
The IUE paid is a credit against the IT.

instruments.explanation: The corporate income tax. Collections grew sharply in 2025 (about 44% in January–October).
exceptions: Public universities, non-profits and some regional promotion zones are exempt.

taxes.base: Gross income earned from commerce, industry, professions, rental of goods, works and services.
taxes.payer: All natural and legal persons carrying out the taxed activity.

rate.headline: 3% of gross income
details: Creditable against the IUE, so it works as a minimum tax on turnover.

instruments.explanation: A turnover tax typical of Bolivia's reliance on indirect taxes.
exceptions: Wages, exports, interest on savings and some public services are excluded.

names.official: Régimen Complementario al Impuesto al Valor Agregado (RC-IVA)

taxes.base: Income of individuals from capital and work (salaried and independent), net of allowances.

rate.headline: 13% of taxable income, offset by IVA on invoices
details: Taxpayers credit 13% of the invoices they collect, which mostly cancels the tax, giving it a monitoring function.
Decree 5503 of December 2025 lets taxpayers discount an extra 20% of the IVA on 'Made in Bolivia' purchases until December 2027.

instruments.explanation: Bolivia's personal income tax; it collects little because invoices offset it.
exceptions: Wages up to a threshold of minimum-wage multiples are not taxed.

taxes.base: Alcohol, tobacco, soft drinks, vehicles and other specific goods.

rate.headline: Ad valorem or specific rates by product
details: Rates are listed by product in the law and its regulations.

instruments.explanation: The selective excise tax on consumption goods.

rate.headline: 32% of production value (plus 18% royalties and participations)
details: The 32% IDH sits on top of 18% royalties and participations (11% departmental, 1% national compensatory, 6% for the state company YPFB), making a 50% take on upstream production.

instruments.explanation: A legal 'tax' on hydrocarbons, functionally a resource rent. Its proceeds are shared with departments, municipalities and universities.
exceptions: Distribution of proceeds follows the Hydrocarbons Law and later decrees.

instruments.statusNote: The fuel-subsidy removal in Decreto Supremo 5503 (December 2025) changed fuel pricing and the fiscal role of the IEHD; check the current fuel price schedule before relying on any amount.

names.official: Impuesto Especial a los Hidrocarburos y sus Derivados (IEHD)
names.native: Impuesto Especial a los Hidrocarburos y sus Derivados

taxes.base: Sales of gasoline, diesel and other hydrocarbon derivatives in the domestic market, by volume.

rate.headline: Fixed boliviano amount per litre by product
details: Set by decree and shared with departments and other beneficiaries.

instruments.explanation: A per-litre tax on fuels that, until 2025, was small because fuel prices were subsidised.
exceptions: Special regimes for some uses such as aviation.

instruments.statusNote: The government announced the elimination of the ITF in November 2025 and the SIN reported on 14 April 2026 that RND 102600000013 abrogated its regulation, ending withholding on US-dollar bank operations. Confirm whether the underlying Law 3446 has been repealed.

taxes.base: Debits and credits in foreign-currency accounts above a threshold.

rate.headline: Small percentage of US-dollar operations – being eliminated
details: Historically 0.15%–0.20% of foreign-currency transactions over the threshold.

instruments.explanation: A tax on dollar transactions introduced to encourage the use of bolivianos.
exceptions: Transactions in bolivianos were not taxed.

instruments.statusNote: Law 1357 (2020) is the statute in the SIN's October 2025 table of taxes in force. The government announced its elimination in November 2025; a repeal proposal was still before the Legislative Assembly in March 2026. Verify the current status.

taxes.base: Net wealth of individuals above Bs 30 million on 31 December.
taxes.payer: Very wealthy resident and non-resident individuals.

rate.headline: 1.4% / 1.9% / 2.4% above Bs 30 million
details: 1.4% on net wealth from Bs 30,000,001 to 40 million; 1.9% from 40,000,001 to 50 million; 2.4% above 50 million.

instruments.explanation: A wealth tax created in 2020 that only a few hundred people were liable for.

taxes.base: Customs value of imported goods by tariff item.

rate.headline: Ad valorem rates by tariff item
details: Preferential rates apply within the Andean Community, Mercosur agreements and other trade agreements.

instruments.explanation: Duties collected by the Aduana Nacional, separate from the SIN.
exceptions: Exemptions for capital goods and inputs in some sectors.

names.official: Aportes a la seguridad social de largo y corto plazo (pensiones y salud)

rate.headline: Employer and worker shares set by the Pensions Law and the health-insurance regime
details: Long-term pensions are managed by the Gestora Pública de la Seguridad Social; short-term health insurance by the Caja Nacional de Salud and other funds.

instruments.explanation: Compulsory contributions that are not taxes; they are not administered by the SIN.
exceptions: Independent workers have separate contribution rules.

names.official: Regalías departamentales por hidrocarburos y minería

taxes.base: Value of hydrocarbons and minerals extracted in the department.

rate.headline: 11% of hydrocarbon production value; mining royalty by mineral and price
details: The 11% departmental hydrocarbon royalty goes to the producing department; the mining royalty (regalía minera) percentages depend on the mineral and its price under the Mining Law.

instruments.explanation: The main own revenue of producing departments. It is payment for state-owned resources, not a tax.
exceptions: Non-producing departments receive compensatory transfers instead.

names.official: Impuestos departamentales autorizados por la Ley 154 (transmisión gratuita de bienes; propiedad de aeronaves y embarcaciones)

taxes.base: Inheritance and donations of registrable assets; ownership of motor vehicles for air and water navigation.

rate.headline: Set by each department if it creates the tax
details: Ley 154 lets departments create these taxes; few have done so.

instruments.explanation: Departments have almost no own tax base; these are the only taxes the law assigns to them.
exceptions: A department cannot tax bases assigned to the central or municipal domains.

taxes.base: Services and licences provided by the departmental government.

rate.headline: Varies by department and service
details: Set by departmental law within the limits of Ley 154 and Ley 031.

exceptions: Fees must relate to an actual service.

names.official: Impuesto a la Propiedad de Bienes Inmuebles (IPBI)
names.native: Impuesto a la Propiedad de Bienes Inmuebles

taxes.base: Assessed value of urban and rural real estate.

rate.headline: Progressive scale of about 0.35% to 1.5% of assessed value
details: The scale is set in law and applied by municipalities; low-value homes are exempt.

exceptions: State property, churches and other institutions are exempt.

names.official: Impuesto a la Propiedad de Vehículos Automotores (IPVA)
names.native: Impuesto a la Propiedad de Vehículos Automotores

taxes.base: Depreciated value of registered land motor vehicles.

rate.headline: Percentage of vehicle value set in the tax scale
details: Applies the scale of Ley 843 to the taxable value, with depreciation by age.

instruments.explanation: An annual municipal tax on vehicle ownership.
exceptions: Public transport and some vehicles get reductions.

names.official: Impuesto Municipal a las Transferencias de Inmuebles y Vehículos Automotores (IMT)

taxes.base: Onerous transfers of real estate and vehicles.
taxes.payer: The seller (or as set by the municipal law).

rate.headline: 3% on real estate; 1.5% on vehicles
details: Municipalities that have not passed their own IMT law leave transfers to be taxed under the IT.

instruments.explanation: A municipal tax on transfers of property.
exceptions: Inheritance and gifts follow other rules.

taxes.base: Municipal services (waste, cemeteries, markets) and licences to operate businesses.

rate.headline: Varies by municipality and service
details: Set by municipal law.

instruments.explanation: Charges for municipal services and business licences, called tasas and patentes.
exceptions: Must be tied to a service or licence.
